title: Channel Partner Registration in Real Estate: Steps, Documents, Terms
seoTitle: Channel Partner Registration: Steps and Documents
excerpt: Channel partner registration in real estate: RERA agent registration, documents developers ask for, the CP agreement and payout terms to check first.

faqs.question: How do I register as a channel partner with a builder?
faqs.answer: First register as a real estate agent with your state RERA authority. Then fill in the builder's CP registration form with your PAN, address proof, photo, bank details, RERA certificate and GST details if any, sign its CP agreement, and get your CP code before you register any buyer.

faqs.question: Is RERA registration required to become a channel partner?
faqs.answer: Yes. Section 9 of the RERA Act, 2016 says an agent cannot facilitate a sale in a registered project without registering with the state authority, and developers ask for the certificate before empanelment. You need a separate registration in each state where you sell registered projects.

faqs.question: What documents are needed for channel partner registration?
faqs.answer: Usually your RERA agent certificate, PAN card, office address proof, a photograph and a cancelled cheque or passbook for payouts. Add a GST certificate if you are registered for GST, and a partnership deed, LLP agreement or incorporation certificate plus an authorisation letter if you register as a firm.

faqs.question: How much does RERA agent registration cost?
faqs.answer: It depends on the state. UP RERA's rules set ₹25,000 for an individual and ₹2,50,000 for a firm. HARERA Gurugram lists ₹50,000 and ₹2,50,000, and MahaRERA ₹10,000 and ₹1,00,000 plus GST. UP also requires a paid four-day training course before you apply.

faqs.question: Is there a fee to register with a developer as a CP?
faqs.answer: The developer terms we reviewed list documents and conditions but no registration fee. Your main cost is the RERA agent registration. Be careful with anyone asking for money to get you empanelled, and confirm the process directly on the developer's official website or with its sales office.

faqs.question: What should I check in a channel partner agreement?
faqs.answer: Check the lead validity period, the rules for accompanying the first site visit, the payout milestone, how many days payment takes, what happens on cancellation, whether commission is on the basic price or full value, rules for self-bookings, and what marketing material you may use without written approval.

faqs.question: When does a channel partner get paid brokerage?
faqs.answer: When the milestone in the CP agreement is met. Published terms vary: one developer pays after the customer has paid 50% of the price, within 30 working days of the invoice; another pays after full dues are received and the property is registered, within 45 days.

faqs.question: How long is a channel partner lead valid?
faqs.answer: It is set by each developer. One Mumbai developer's published terms register the customer to the partner for 90 days, while a Chennai developer keeps a lead valid for 15 days after a site visit. Register every buyer before the first visit and save the confirmation.

faqs.question: Can I register with more than one developer?
faqs.answer: Yes. Channel partners usually work with several developers, and each one has its own empanelment form, CP code and agreement. Your RERA agent registration covers the whole state, so one number works for every developer whose registered projects are in that state.
